**Iceland plans domestic account-to-account scheme to reduce card network dependency**

*A procurement process is under way for infrastructure that would give Icelandic consumers and merchants a payment option outside Visa and Mastercard for the first time.*

The Central Bank of Iceland has begun procuring the core technology for a new domestic account-to-account payment scheme, built on request-to-pay messaging and the country's existing instant credit transfer infrastructure. Tomas Brynjolfsson, the central bank's deputy governor for financial stability, set out the plan at the MoneyLIVE Nordic Banking conference in Copenhagen on October 30, framing it as a response to Iceland's near-total dependence on two international card networks for retail payments.

Iceland's payments landscape is highly digital but unusually concentrated. Virtually all retail transactions run through Visa and Mastercard, a structure the central bank says creates operational and strategic vulnerabilities, particularly if connectivity to external infrastructure is disrupted. The new scheme would allow customers to pay directly from bank accounts in shops, online and in person-to-person transfers. The central bank would provide shared infrastructure, operating standards and settlement, while leaving customer-facing products to commercial banks and payment firms.

The domestic scheme is separate from Iceland's planned participation in the Eurosystem's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement service, agreed with the ECB in June, which has a readiness target in the second half of 2028. Brynjolfsson was explicit that payment sovereignty for a small economy does not mean self-sufficiency but rather ensuring alternatives exist alongside international networks. The initiative mirrors debates playing out across the Nordics and the wider European payments landscape over resilience, sovereignty and the role of domestic rails.

*Sources: [Iceland prepares for domestic account-to-account payments infrastructure](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48698/iceland-prepares-for-domestic-account-to-account-payments-infrastructure) — Finextra*

**EPC publishes updated verification of payee matching recommendations**

*Updated rules on character handling and beneficiary name assessment sharpen the matching logic that underpins Europe's fraud prevention regime for instant payments.*

The European Payments Council (EPC) has published an updated set of recommendations for matching processes under its verification of payee scheme. The guidance covers how payment service providers should handle character variations and assess beneficiary names before initiating a payment, adding specificity to a process that has been live for barely a year.

Verification of payee is a core element of the EU's instant payments regulation, requiring providers to check whether the name given by the payer matches the account holder before executing a transfer. The scheme's effectiveness depends on consistent matching logic across providers and jurisdictions. Divergent implementations have been a recurring concern since the rules took effect, and the EPC's updated recommendations aim to narrow the scope for inconsistency.

The publication comes as the industry continues to grapple with the operational detail of payee verification, with key IBAN-level errors still slipping through the system. More granular matching guidance should reduce false negatives that let fraudulent payments proceed and false positives that block legitimate ones. Uniform adoption across providers remains the outstanding question.

*Sources: [EPC publishes new Verification of Payee matching recommendations](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48697/epc-publishes-new-verification-of-payee-matching-recommendations?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**EU and Canada agree to link real-time payment systems**

*The commitment to connect SEPA instant payments with Canada's Real-Time Rail opens a new corridor for cross-border account-to-account settlement between the two economies.*

The European Union and Canada have committed to connecting their real-time payment systems, and to exploring mutual market access for banks and fintechs. The agreement covers linking SEPA instant payments infrastructure with Canada's Real-Time Rail, which is scheduled to launch in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Cross-border interlinking of domestic instant payment schemes has moved from theoretical to operational in the past year, with the ECB's TIPS platform already supporting cross-currency settlement between the euro area and Scandinavian markets. The EU-Canada commitment extends this logic across the Atlantic, though the technical and regulatory complexity of bridging two distinct currency zones and regulatory frameworks is substantial.

The agreement also includes provisions for reciprocal market access. If implemented, European payment firms could gain a clearer route into the Canadian market, and vice versa. The practical timeline and governance arrangements are not yet specified, but the political commitment signals that both sides see payment system interoperability as part of broader trade and economic cooperation.

*Sources: [EU and Canada plan to link real-time payment systems](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48692/eu-and-canada-plan-to-link-real-time-payment-systems?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**InvestEngine reports 98% success rate with commercial variable recurring payments**

*A 98% success rate from a live deployment offers the first substantial evidence that commercial variable recurring payments can match or exceed card reliability for recurring financial services payments.*

InvestEngine has reported a 98% payment success rate using commercial variable recurring payments (VRP) as an open banking payment method. Nick Oeen, head of product for payments at InvestEngine, disclosed the figure at Open Banking Expo UK and Europe 2026.

Commercial VRP has been positioned as the open banking successor to card-on-file for subscription and recurring payments, but adoption has been held back by questions about reliability and conversion rates compared with cards. A 98% success rate from a live deployment in financial services is rare. For context, card payment success rates for recurring transactions typically sit in a similar range, though they benefit from decades of retry logic and network-level optimisation.

The result is particularly relevant as the UK Payments Initiative and commercial VRP frameworks continue to scale. Sceptics have argued that open banking payment methods cannot yet match card reliability in production. InvestEngine's figures suggest that for at least some use cases, that gap has effectively closed.

*Sources: [InvestEngine achieves 98% payment success rate with commercial VRP](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/investengine-achieves-98-payment-success-rate-with-commercial-vrp/) — Openbankingexpo*

**Stripe launches Treasury product in the UK market**

*UK platforms can now hold, move and manage operational cash from the same Stripe dashboard they use to accept payments, intensifying competition with banking-as-a-service providers.*

Stripe has launched its Treasury product in the UK, enabling platform customers to manage funds from the same dashboard they use to accept payments. The product lets founders hold, move and manage money without needing a separate banking relationship for operational cash.

Stripe Treasury has been available in the US since 2020, where it is offered in partnership with banks that hold the underlying deposits. The UK launch extends the same embedded finance model into a market where banking-as-a-service competition is already intense, with providers such as Modulr, ClearBank and Griffin operating in the same space.

Platforms built on Stripe's payment stack gain integrated cash management without additional operational friction. Stripe's existing merchant base already uses its payment rails, making Treasury a natural upsell rather than a standalone product requiring its own acquisition effort. That distribution advantage poses a direct challenge to banking-as-a-service incumbents, which must win platform relationships from scratch.

*Sources: [Stripe Treasury launches in the UK](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/111563/stripe-treasury-launches-in-the-uk?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
